elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Company may assign this Agreement, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate..." — express no-consent affiliate assignment for Customer.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence: "...or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" without HDI's consent — all three trigger events named.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent" — direct prohibition on Vendor assignment absent Customer consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" attaches the reasonableness standard to the Vendor-assignment consent.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and may not in any event assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Company" — absolute bar, not curable by consent language.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "A change of control of the Company shall not give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement."

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The insertion is asymmetric: Customer may assign to a successor without consent, but HDI "may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent," so Vendor has no free successor right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears anywhere in the rendered clause; Customer's successor assignment is unconditional and Vendor's is consent-gated, not notice-based.
A retained no-consent non-successor exception survives — Customer may assign to an affiliate "without HDI's consent" — which defeats a universal consent requirement for other assignments.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The only consent gate created (Vendor assignment) is qualified: "which shall not be unreasonably withheld." The condition applies only to that gate and carries the reasonableness standard.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted paragraph after 10.3; the position is complete at the preferred level, so the incomplete fallback checklist is immaterial.

Fallback is not complete: no written-notice mechanic, no mutual successor right, and Customer's affiliate carve-out is a retained no-consent non-successor exception that defeats "Other assignments require consent."

Minimality holds: the original binding-effect sentence in 10.3 is retained verbatim with no deletions or paraphrase, and the insertion is a concise three-sentence clause containing only checklist content (affiliate/successor carve-out, Vendor consent plus reasonableness, competitor bar, change-of-control no-termination). No survival tail, expense, notice-procedure, or damages boilerplate was added.

Intent is preserved: the edit creates no new Vendor assignment exception (it restricts Vendor), leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and the retained "successors and assigns" binding-effect language is consistent with the new permitted/prohibited transfer mechanics.
No broad "notwithstanding" override was used; the drafter used a direct "without HDI's consent" permission, which is the minimal formulation.
Classification as a deviation is supportable: Section 10.3 as drafted is a binding-effect provision only and satisfies no fallback element, so it fails the fallback on material terms.
